entry.title: Feed Reader

scenario.name: Feed Reader
scenario.audience: One individual reader running a self-hosted feed reader service on their own server, following about twenty blogs and news feeds.
scenario.objective: Keep a personal list of feeds, let new items arrive on their own, and clear the unread backlog each morning while keeping the list portable
workflow: Add sources: submit a site or feed URL, or import an OPML file, placing each feed in a category; the user's list is the only selector of what may appear.

Intake: the background scheduler refreshes each subscribed feed on its own interval (default polling 1h, honoring feed TTL and ETag/Last-Modified), parses RSS, Atom or JSON Feed, and stores newly published items attributed to their feed with status unread.
Triage: open the Unread view to see what arrived, with per-feed and total unread counts, then open an item to read it in the reader view with previous/next navigation through already-read items.
Record state: mark entries read (one by one, per feed or category, or mark all as read) and star the keepers, since starred is a separate flag from unread/read.
Maintain: export the subscription list as OPML to carry it to another reader, and re-import that file to restore the same feeds.

capabilities: Standing intake of the user's own list: a background scheduler refreshes each subscribed feed on its own interval (default 1h, raised by feed TTL, Cache-Control and Expires, never lowered below the configured interval), honours ETag/Last-Modified, parses RSS, Atom or JSON Feed and stores each newly published item once, attributed to its feed and unread.

Personal subscription list management: the operator's own list of sources grouped into categories, filled by a feed URL, by a site URL that advertises a feed, or by an OPML import, and the only selector of what may appear on the reading surface.
Triage surface with per feed and total unread counts, an unread view over the selected scope and a reader view that opens one item with previous/next navigation through already-read items.
Reading state recording: mark entries read one by one, per feed, per category or for the whole account, and star the keepers with a flag that stays independent of unread and read.
List portability: export the subscription list as OPML with one outline per feed inside its category outline, and re-import that file to restore the same subscriptions without duplicates.
limits: The upstream reference was read as source only and was never built, installed or run; no upstream runtime behaviour is claimed and no certification of the upstream product is made.
The probe drives the JSON API of the target; the operator-facing HTML surface described in the architecture is verified by hand and is not asserted by an acceptance case.
Only RSS 2.0 fixtures are exercised by the probe; Atom 0.3/1.0 and JSON Feed 1.0/1.1 parsing is specified in the contract but not covered by an acceptance case.

The scheduled intake check of A01 is reported as not_run when the service does not report polling_interval_seconds on GET /api/v1/config, or when the configured polling interval is longer than the probe intake timeout; the remaining A01 sub-checks then run on the explicit refresh endpoint instead of the scheduler path.

The probe requires a disposable instance because read-all is account wide: it refuses to run against an instance that already holds subscriptions outside its own probe- categories, and it deletes only feeds in those categories and categories whose title starts with probe-.
The site URL discovery reads only the link rel=alternate tags of the page; it does not crawl the page body and does not guess a feed path.
Full text extraction, rewrite and filter rules, share codes, webhooks, third party integrations and the Fever or Google Reader compatible APIs are outside this leaf and are not implemented.
Podcast and video enclosures, playback position and per feed crawler mode are not part of the target scope.
The reader view renders the stored item content only; the target never re-fetches the article page, so an item whose source page changes is not updated in place.
Multi user accounts, per user API tokens and password or passkey login flows are reduced to a single seeded operator in this scope.
OPML import reuses an existing category by name, so two categories with the same title inside one file are merged into the first match.
